def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (T K : Fm → Fm) (lam : Fm),
    𝓢 ⊢ lam 🡘 ∼T lam →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (lam ⋎ ∼lam) →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (lam ⋎ ∼lam) 🡒 T (lam ⋎ ∼lam) →
    𝓢 ⊢ T (lam ⋎ ∼lam) 🡒 (T lam ⋎ T (∼lam)) →
    𝓢 ⊢ (T lam ⋎ T (∼lam)) 🡒 (T lam 🡘 lam) →
    𝓢 ⊢ ⊥
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm and provability relation for S on Fm, every system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, every pair of functions T, K : Fm → Fm, and every sentence lam in Fm, let E abbreviate lam ⋎ (∼lam). If (1) 𝓢 proves lam 🡘 ∼(T lam), (2) 𝓢 proves K E, (3) 𝓢 proves (K E) 🡒 (T E), (4) 𝓢 proves (T E) 🡒 ((T lam) ⋎ T (∼lam)), and (5) 𝓢 proves ((T lam) ⋎ T (∼lam)) 🡒 ((T lam) 🡘 lam), then 𝓢 proves ⊥. Each hypothesis requires proof of the indicated whole sentence; 🡘 is the conjunction of the two directions of implication inside the language. In (4) and (5), T (∼lam) applies T to the negation of lam, unlike ∼(T lam) in (1). No consistency assumption or general law for T or K is required, and no existence of a sentence satisfying the hypotheses is asserted."}
translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm and provability relation for S on Fm, every system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, every pair of functions T, K : Fm → Fm, and every sentence lam in Fm, let E abbreviate lam ⋎ (∼lam). If (1) 𝓢 proves lam 🡘 ∼(T lam), (2) 𝓢 proves K E, (3) 𝓢 proves (K E) 🡒 (T E), (4) 𝓢 proves (T E) 🡒 ((T lam) ⋎ T (∼lam)), and (5) 𝓢 proves ((T lam) ⋎ T (∼lam)) 🡒 ((T lam) 🡘 lam), then 𝓢 proves ⊥. Each hypothesis requires proof of the indicated whole sentence; 🡘 is the conjunction of the two directions of implication inside the language. In (4) and (5), T (∼lam) applies T to the negation of lam, unlike ∼(T lam) in (1). No consistency assumption or general law for T or K is required, and no existence of a sentence satisfying the hypotheses is asserted.

divergences.description: The passage states that T(λ ∨ ¬λ) is equivalent to T(λ) ∨ T(¬λ). The target assumes only the forward implication, which is the only direction the proof uses.

The target gives a conditional proof for any classical system rather than an inconsistency statement about EA_DT by name. In particular, it takes K(λ ∨ ¬λ) as a hypothesis where the passage obtains it from validity by E1.

judgement.summary: The target captures the quicker proof: E1’s instance, I’s instance, and the forward truth implication yield D(λ) in its unfolded form. The conditioned biconditional then gives T(λ) ↔ λ, which contradicts the liar biconditional λ ↔ ¬T(λ).
